newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ First caucus begins deliberations on coalition.
newsitem.headline: NZ First caucus begins deliberations on coalition.

text.p: Nationalist New Zealand First began a caucus meeting on Friday morning which is expected to be the first in a series to decide the shape of the next government.
A spokesman for NZ First leader Winston Peters said the meeting was not "the caucus" which would make the final decision.

Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with both the caretaker conservative National government and centre-left Labour over the shape of the new government.

NZ First MPs are confident a final decision can be made before parliament sits on December 12, with commentators expecting a small majority of the 17 NZ First MPs to favour a deal with Labour while the leadership is leaning towards National.
The NZ First spokesman said further meetings with at least one of the other parties were planned for Friday afternoon.
Labour has scheduled a special caucus meeting for Saturday and NZ First has told its MPs to be on standby for special caucus meetings.
A spokeswoman for Prime Minister Jim Bolger said National had no caucus meetings planned for the weekend and she was not aware of any formal negotiations with NZ First scheduled for Friday.
